system.name: ZOC
system.one_liner: ZOC's I/O Link mechanism that uses two-dimensional page tables to give the service VM direct DMA access to host and VM memory

components.name: Service VM (as virtual SmartNIC)
components.role: guest whose GPA space is used to construct a two-dimensional mapping of host physical memory

components.name: data-plane I/O address space
components.role: the userspace data plane's view of I/O-accessible address space

components.name: L1 Page Tables
components.role: guest page tables mapping the service VM's GPA-accessible HPA space into the userspace data plane

components.name: hole
components.role: reserved gap in the GPA space left for the service VM's own memory, excluded from the offset-mapped HPA range

components.name: Host OS
components.role: physical memory region belonging to the host OS

components.name: Service VM
components.role: physical memory region belonging to the service VM itself

components.name: User VMs
components.role: physical memory regions belonging to user VMs

components.name: Host
components.role: the physical host's memory view containing the L0 page tables

components.name: L0 Page Tables (e.g., EPT)
components.role: hardware-assisted page tables (e.g., Intel EPT) mapping host physical address space into the service VM's GPA space at a fixed offset

flows.what: host physical address space mapped via L0 page tables at a fixed GPA offset
GPA-accessible HPA space mapped via L1 page tables

content.key_idea: ZOC's I/O Link uses hardware EPT-style L0 page tables to map the host's entire physical address space into the service VM's guest-physical space at a fixed offset, then re-maps it via L1 page tables for the userspace data plane.
content.reading_order: Bottom-up: the Host's L0 page tables and physical regions, mapped diagonally with a fixed offset into the Service VM's L1 page tables and data-plane address space above.

encoding.color_means: tan = Host OS / User VMs physical memory regions, pale blue = the Service VM's own memory region and its GPA-space boxes, pale yellow = the page-table bands themselves
encoding.line_style_means: dotted diagonal lines trace how a physical address region in the Host's L0 page tables maps to the corresponding region in the Service VM's L1 page tables/GPA space; 'Fixed offset' and 'hole' annotate the reserved offset and gap
encoding.emphasis: aligning the Host and Service VM address-space bars vertically, with dotted lines and a 'Fixed offset' callout, pinpoints exactly how the two-dimensional mapping translates one address space into the other
reusable_patterns: two stacked address-space bars connected by dotted correspondence lines to explain a memory-mapping scheme
weaknesses: reusing the label 'Service VM' for both the outer virtual-SmartNIC box and an inner memory-region box could confuse readers
the 'hole' concept is only briefly annotated, without a full caption explaining why it exists

evidence: the I/O Link takes advantage of hardware-assisted L0 page tables, such as Intel EPT
to map the entire host physical address (HPA) space into the service VM's guest physical address (GPA) space
This mapping is performed with a fixed, reserved GPA offset (e.g., 1 TB)

summary: Figure 5 zooms into ZOC's two-dimensional page-table mechanism for DMA inside the I/O Link. It stacks two memory views: the Host's physical memory (bottom), organized by hardware L0 page tables (e.g., Intel EPT) into regions for Host OS, Service VM, and User VMs; and the Service VM's guest-physical memory (top), whose L1 page tables re-expose the same regions to the userspace data-plane I/O address space. A fixed, reserved GPA offset (annotated in red) and a deliberate 'hole' let the service VM address any host physical address X simply by adding the offset, while dotted diagonal lines trace how each host region lands in the guest's address space. The figure uses flat tan/blue/yellow boxes with dashed and dotted lines rather than arrows to emphasize address correspondence over data flow.
